newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak PM rules out crown devaluation - agency.
newsitem.headline: Slovak PM rules out crown devaluation - agency.

text.p: The Slovak crown will not be devalued despite the country's widening trade deficit, although other options to bring the shortfall under control are being considered, Premier Vladimir Meciar said on the weekend.

The official TASR news agency quoted Meciar after an extraordinary meeting of the country's economic ministers as saying recent reports of an imminent devaluation of the crown were little more than speculation.
"Any thoughts of devaluation (of the crown) are pure speculation...a (devaluation) is out of the question," TASR quoted Meciar as saying.
"On the contrary, the central bank's hard currency reserves recently increased by some $200 million, so there is no reason for speculations about devaluation," he added.
Meciar said the government would adopt "other" measures to help eliminate unfavourable developments in the country's foreign trade balance.
"Rather than restrictive tools, these measures would be aimed at bringing Slovakia to a more active position in foreign trade," Meciar said without elaborating.
In the first half of the year Slovakia posted a foreign trade deficit of 26.975 billion crowns, a dramatic reversal from 1.8 billion crown surplus posted for all of 1995.

Slovak officials have said they were not overly concerned with the trade balance so far, saying imports were boosted by large technological and industrial modernisation investments, as well as through the repayment of Russian debts to Slovakia with goods.
Much of the investment has been aimed at the completion of the Mochovce nuclear power plant and the modernisation programme at the country's sole oil refiner Slovnaft.
